title: Finite Hamiltonian carré-du-champ comparison for physical-coordinate likelihood gradients
question: Does the physical-coordinate conditional form track the Hamiltonian-derived kinetic carré-du-champ on the actual Q3 likelihood gradients, after the coordinate-only potential terms are removed by commutation?

new_perspective.principle: Use the kinetic part of the Q3 Hamiltonian as the local gradient generator instead of treating the coordinate Dirichlet form as an arbitrary graph metric.
motivation: For a one-site coordinate multiplier F=f(q), every onsite and spatial potential is a function of commuting q coordinates and has zero commutator with F.
The only Hamiltonian contribution to the first carré-du-champ is therefore the kinetic operator p^2/(2 chi), represented by (2 chi)^(-1) Tr(diag(pi) [p,F]^*[p,F]) in a finite q-coordinate row.
Comparing this form with the R-401 nearest-neighbour physical-coordinate form tests whether the proposed metric is tied to the actual generator rather than only to a truncation geometry.
route: Reconstruct the finite Q3 Gibbs state, every split-history prefix and both history adjoints from the R-399 fixture.
For every oriented collar row, form the conditional coordinate law pi and the actual likelihood multiplier f=q_prefix/p_prefix.
Compute D_q(f)=sum min(pi_k,pi_(k+1))*((f_(k+1)-f_k)/(x_(k+1)-x_k))^2 and E_kin(f)=(2 chi)^(-1) Tr(diag(pi)[p,F]^*[p,F]) in the q basis.
Verify that coordinate-only onsite and bond potentials commute with F, and report the finite ratio E_kin/D_q without treating it as a uniform constant.
Repeat both orientations, source/history signs, split orders, prefixes and adjoints, then use a momentum-to-coordinate hostile mutation to show the kinetic identification is load-bearing.
new_perspective.qft_bridge: A uniform two-sided comparison E_kin approximately D_q on an invariant common core could connect R-401 to the Hamiltonian shell estimate. The finite package supplies no such analytic comparison, cutoff/volume/phase uniformity, common alpha, OS/KMS/GNS dynamics, gap, continuum, C6, Sector-A or Pre-A closure.

finite_theorem.kinetic_form: E_kin(f)=(2 chi)^(-1) Tr(diag(pi)[p,F]^*[p,F]), F=diag(f) in the q eigenbasis
finite_theorem.potential_isolation: [V(q_0,...,q_{V-1}),F_s]=0 for every finite coordinate polynomial V
finite_theorem.comparison: The finite ratio E_kin/D_q is reported only on nonconstant rows; no uniform lower or upper comparison is assumed.

lean_crosscheck.boundary: Lean checks only scalar positivity and the algebraic commuting/potential isolation skeleton; finite matrices, Gibbs rows, form comparison and all regulator or QFT limits remain in the executable evidence boundary.

promotion_criteria: Prove an analytic two-sided comparison between E_kin and D_q on a cutoff-independent Hamiltonian-derived common core.
Prove the comparison uniformly in source, volume, cutoff, phase, orientation and exhaustion shape.
Only then combine the form comparison with the R-399 conditional transfer and pursue common-alpha or OS/KMS identification.
stop_conditions: If E_kin/D_q collapses or diverges systematically with cutoff, retain R-401 only as a diagnostic and register the comparison obstruction before substitution.
If the comparison depends on beta, history or orientation, keep it as a finite parameterized interface and do not promote uniformity.
If the finite potential commutator isolation fails outside the declared coordinate-multiplier class, restrict the route and do not claim full Hamiltonian locality.
boundary: T0 claim-nonbearing finite Hamiltonian carré-du-champ comparison only. It proves no cutoff-, volume-, source-, phase- or shape-uniform form comparison, no invariant common core, no common alpha, no OS/KMS/GNS reconstruction, no mass gap, no continuum, C6, Sector-A or Pre-A closure.
no_overclaim: A finite kinetic commutator form and a finite coordinate Dirichlet form are two different quadratic forms. Their observed ratio is a diagnostic, not an analytic comparison theorem or a Q3 real-time locality result.
